chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washha from Al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is nothing except that it has a limit. I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, so what is the limit of reliance (tawakkul)?' He said, 'Conviction (yaqin).' I said, 'So what is the limit of conviction?' He said, 'Not fearing anything along with Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What is the limit of reliance (tawakkul) and conviction (yaqin) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the metaphysical boundaries of spiritual states, defining the limit of *tawakkul* (reliance) as *yaqin* (firm conviction) and the limit of *yaqin* as the absence of fear alongside Allah. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on inner certainty as the true measure of reliance, distinguishing it from mere verbal declaration. It reflects the broader theological principle that true monotheism (*tawhid*) requires the heart to be anchored solely in Divine power, free from auxiliary anxieties.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washha, from Al Musna Bin Al Waleed, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘There is nothing except that there is a limit for it’.

I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! So what is the limit of the reliance (upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: الْيَقِينَ ‘The conviction’. I said, ‘So what is the limit of the conviction?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Not fearing anything along with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from al-Muthanna ibn al-Walid from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once said, ‘There is nothing without a limit.’

I (the narrator) then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what is the limit of trust?’ The Imam said, ‘It is certainty.’ 1 then asked, ‘What is the limit of certainty?’ The Imam said, ‘It is when, with having Allah on your side, you do not fear anything.’”
